title: Warsaw’s turning points, with a historian of its ruin
description: Travel journalist Paul Bloomfield talks to historian Alexandra Richie, author of a history of the 1944 Uprising, on the turning points of Warsaw’s past. The Barbican, a 16th-century gate tower rebuilt after 1945, guards the Old Town’s north side.

title: A republic that elected its kings
spotify: In Our Time The Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth
apple: In Our Time The Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth
description: Melvyn Bragg and guests on the union of Poland and Lithuania, formalised in 1569, whose nobles elected their kings. One of them, Jan III Sobieski, victor over the Ottomans at Vienna in 1683, built Wilanów Palace as his summer residence.

title: The Rolling Stones play behind the Iron Curtain
place: Congress Hall, Palace of Culture and Science
spotify: Stories From The Eastern West STONES
description: Culture.pl’s podcast on the Rolling Stones’ April 1967 concert in Warsaw, one of the first by a Western rock band in the Soviet bloc. Fans without tickets clashed with police outside the Congress Hall, the venue inside Stalin’s Palace of Culture.

title: Smuggling children out of the ghetto
episode: The woman who saved 2,500 children from the Warsaw ghetto
spotify: Witness History The woman who saved 2,500 children from the Warsaw ghetto
description: Irena Sendler, a Catholic social worker, used her pass into the Warsaw ghetto to smuggle out Jewish children for Żegota, the underground aid council, and buried their names in jars. A stretch of the ghetto wall survives in a courtyard off Sienna Street.

title: A ghetto fighter who led survivors out through the sewers
description: Simha ‘Kazik’ Rotem, who guided fighters out through the sewers as the Germans crushed the 1943 Warsaw Ghetto Uprising, tells his story. The mound at Miła 18 marks the bunker where the uprising’s commander, Mordechai Anielewicz, died.

title: Students against the censors, March 1968
description: After the authorities banned a staging of Adam Mickiewicz’s play ‘Forefathers’ Eve’, University of Warsaw students rallied for free speech in March 1968 and were beaten by police. Their protests began at the university’s gate on Krakowskie Przedmieście.

title: The plane crash that killed a president
description: In April 2010 a plane carrying President Lech Kaczyński and 95 others crashed near Smolensk in Russia, on the way to a Katyn massacre commemoration. Radosław Sikorski, then foreign minister, recalls the day. A memorial stands on Piłsudski Square.

title: Teenage scouts in the 1944 Uprising
spotify: Witness History Scouts in the Warsaw Uprising
description: A former scout recalls the Warsaw Uprising of 1944, the Home Army’s revolt against German occupation, in which boys and girls ran messages, mail and ammunition. The Little Insurgent statue on Podwale Street honours the child fighters.
